script: Why did FIFA just fire one of their most important members? Meet Kevin Lamour. He was FIFA's Chief Operating Officer, the third most powerful person in the entire organization, and one of President Gianni Infantino's most trusted allies. These two go way back because they worked together at UEFA, and Lamour even helped campaign for Infantino to become FIFA president back in 2016. But the thing that would tear their friendship apart was hidden inside a plan almost nobody was supposed to see. In late July, FIFA quietly announced a plan called FIFA Forward Enterprise, and the idea was to sell off about 20% of a new company that would control the rights to the World Cup, valuing it at $20 billion dollars. Basically, they wanted to hand a piece of the biggest tournament on the planet over to private investors. Lamour was furious, so he went public and told the Associated Press that staff had been deceived and that this was the project of just one person, adding that if speaking out cost him his job, so be it. But saying those words out loud lit a fuse that reached all the way to the top. The deal was already falling apart because UEFA's 55 member nations had voted to threaten a full boycott of future World Cups. Then Lamour spoke out from the inside, and that same night Infantino was forced to scrap the whole thing. 17 days later, FIFA fired Kevin Lamour. So the reason one of FIFA's most important members got fired is simple: he told the truth about selling the World Cup, it worked, and the people in charge made sure he paid for it.
